name: Idle Detection
plain: Tells a site when the person is away from keyboard and mouse or the screen is locked.
meaning: Reveals when the person is present: active or idle (at least 60 seconds) and whether the screen is locked. Useful for chat presence; also shows daily schedule, sleep and work hours.

access.prompt_ui: Chrome prompt Know when you are actively using your device, Allow or Block; needs a user gesture.

limits.headline: Can tell when you step away or lock your screen, if you allow it
limits.user_action: You tap a button like Show my status and tap Allow
can: See whether you are active or idle for at least 60 seconds
See if your screen is locked
Show presence in chat or reset a shared kiosk
Keep checking while the page is open
cannot: Work before you tap Allow in Chrome
Work in Firefox, Safari or on iPhone
See what you are doing, only whether you are active or away
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge on computers and Android ask first. Firefox, Safari and iPhone browsers do not support it.

story.what_it_is: A site can learn when you step away from the keyboard and mouse or lock your screen.

marketing.name: Idle Detection API
marketing.pitch: Lets a page know when a user is idle or the screen is locked, after the user allows it.

story.for_you: A prompt asks to know when you are idle. If you allow it, the site can show you as away in chat or pause things. You never see the checks themselves.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to show presence in chat and team tools, and to save resources. It is also a window into when you are at your desk. That is why it needs a clear allow.

use_cases.example: A web chat shows a friend as Away after they leave their computer, so you know not to expect a reply.
A shared support desk marks agents as idle and sends new tickets to those at their desks.
A browser game lobby pauses a match search when you walk away, so teammates are not left waiting.
A live auction site logs out an idle bidder to protect their account.
A banking site locks the page when it sees the device screen is locked and idle.
A test platform notes that a student has left their screen, as a sign of cheating risk.
A video site pauses autoplay of the next episode when no one is there to watch.

abuse: Learning when the person is away from the computer
